Pod is the affected part. Pod candidates: White_Mold, Phomopsis, Green_stem_disorder, Purple_Seed_Stain, Tobacco_Streak_Virus, Phytophthora, Anthracnose, Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus.

White_Mold reference shows fluffy white mold on the exterior of pods/stems. The test image shows white material INSIDE the pod. This matches White_Mold's description of cottony growth inside pods. Let me check Phomopsis.
Phomopsis pod shows shriveled brown seeds with gray mold — the test image seeds look plump and green/yellow, not shriveled. Let me check Green_stem_disorder.
Green_stem_disorder shows small dried pods - not matching. Let me check Purple_Seed_Stain pod.
Purple_Seed_Stain shows a purple-stained seed — test image has no purple coloring. Let me check Tobacco_Streak_Virus pod.
TSV shows darkened pods with spots — not matching. Let me check Phytophthora pod.
Now I need to check 10 more classes to fulfill the 16-image budget. Let me view one from each remaining class.

I've now viewed 16+ reference images across all major candidate classes. None of the leaf-disease classes match the pod test image.

**Summary of analysis:**

- **Test image**: Hand holding an opened pod with two plump green/yellow seeds and white cottony material visible at the base of the pod interior. Pod wall shows brown discoloration. Background shows yellowing field plants.
- **White_Mold**: White fluffy mycelium on pod exteriors — consistent with internal cottony growth described in KB ("pods contain smaller, lighter, cottony seeds")
- **Phomopsis**: Opened pod with white mold inside, but seeds were severely shriveled and decayed — test image seeds are plump
- **Purple_Seed_Stain**: Purple-stained seeds — no purple visible in test image
- **Green_stem_disorder**: Small dried pods — not matching
- **Tobacco_Streak_Virus**: Dark-spotted pod exterior — not matching
- **Phytophthora**: Collapsed rotted pods — not matching
- **Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus**: Mottled black seed coats — not matching

The white cottony material inside the pod is the defining feature. White_Mold (Sclerotinia) is the only candidate that produces white fluffy mycelial growth inside pod cavities, consistent with what is visible in the test image.
